canonical_semantics.clarification: Read current lookup.clarification {assessment_id,assessment_version,question,response_allowed,grants_implementation_authority:false}. Upstream validates current verified source/environment, credential allowlist, automatic assessment, issuer/subject/project/environment ownership, source_revision, current immutable assessment, no started implementation, and no native archive. First answer durably records input and prepares a read-only continuation. Exact trimmed answer/assessment/version/principal replay returns the saved continuation without enqueueing again; prior replay can succeed even after cancellation/archive. Different answer is 409 conflict; outdated/new answers after cancellation or native archive are 409 stale. Source revision change is 409. Reporter dismiss changes history visibility only. Saved answer with blocked assessment remains answered with a native recovery warning; never create replacement work.
canonical_semantics.subscription: Explicit notify_on_resolution=true; consent_version defaults upstream to v1. Both routes verify ownership and derive email from the current Known User proof; missing configured email is 403 feedback_notification_identity_email_required. They return HTTP 201 even for an existing active subscription (created=false). Dedup key is project/report_kind/report_id/normalized verified email. No subscription ID, reusable credential, callback URL, background authorization, readiness or notification delivery receipt is returned. Cancellation/archive do not revoke existing consent or necessarily block subscribing; this must not be interpreted as ready.
canonical_semantics.custody: Handrail feedback-reporter-notifications owns fixed-lifecycle email selection, release-evidence evaluation, delivery claiming/deduplication and sending. MCP only transports consent. Email readiness and the Agent SDK canonicalFeedbackReady predicate are distinct; preserve the existing SDK predicate for conversation readiness.
canonical_semantics.uncertainty: All feedback HTTP calls are single-attempt. Timeout/network failure/unreadable success does not prove non-application. Keep original principal/runtime, canonical report ID, submission event_id/idempotency_key, and clarification assessment tuple/answer. Reconcile with the existing SDK effect/receipt mechanism; no automatic replacement or new identity. New distinct scope is a new authorized intent, not an exact retry.

background_authorization_gap.evidence: The canonical subscription routes return only email consent status and require a currently verified application session on each call. They provide no token exchange, durable observation grant, refresh token or conversation callback.
background_authorization_gap.next_step: Avery must bind the existing SDK withClient to an already authorized fresh Known User session path for each observation; if Mills has no such background path, keep unattended conversation observation as an explicit upstream dependency. Do not retain raw sessions/cookies or treat email subscription as that grant.
